hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: A binary tree is stable if each non-leaf node value equals the sum of its immediate children.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Process subtrees recursively from leaves upward using post-order tree exploration.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Calculate the discrepancy at each node and add the necessary modifications to a cumulative total.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right

def minOperationsToStabilize(root: TreeNode) -> int:
    ops = 0

    def dfs(node: TreeNode) -> int:
        nonlocal ops
        if not node:
            return 0
        if not node.left and not node.right:
            return node.val

        l_val = dfs(node.left)
        r_val = dfs(node.right)
        child_sum = l_val + r_val

        ops += abs(node.val - child_sum)
        return child_sum

    dfs(root)
    return ops
```
